name: Terrisa Bukovinac
bio: Terrisa Bukovinac is an anti-abortion activist who founded Pro-Life San Francisco in 2017 and the Progressive Anti-Abortion Uprising in 2021, and served as president of Democrats for Life of America starting in 2020. She ran in the 2024 Democratic presidential primary, receiving about 2.7% of the vote in New Jersey. She is running as an independent in New Jersey's 9th district.

platform.point: Makes ending abortion the center of her campaign, describing it as genocide.
Presents resisting fascism as her second main campaign theme.
Advocates a federal abortion ban, defunding Planned Parenthood and repealing the FACE Act.
Supports lowering the cost of childbirth and expanding parental leave.

welfare.evidence: Backs lowering the cost of giving birth and expanding parental leave, a specific but limited family-support stance.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, supports a federal ban, fetal personhood and repealing the FACE Act; no stated positions found on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech.

notes: Searched the campaign site (a single page with no issue pages), Wikipedia and 2023 campaign-launch coverage; beyond abortion and family costs, no stated positions on economy, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech, education or faith were found. The liberty score still rests on abortion alone.

name: Lynn Chapman
bio: Lynn Chapman is the Independent American Party of Nevada's nominee for the 2nd congressional district, a seat she also sought in 2024. She has lobbied at the Nevada Legislature since 1987, served the party as state treasurer and national committeeman, and was state vice president of Nevada Families for Freedom. She has also served on the Nevada Home Educators board and the state Home School Advisory Board.

platform.point: Gathered signatures for Nevada petition drives aimed at cutting taxes.
Worked on a petition drive to define marriage as between a man and a woman.
Helped change Nevada's home-school laws and served on the state Home School Advisory Board.
Backed a petition to bar government employees from serving in two branches of government at once.

economy.evidence: Took part in Nevada petition drives to cut taxes, per a profile posted by her party.

liberty.evidence: On LGBTQ issues, worked on a petition to define marriage as between a man and a woman; no positions found on abortion, drugs, guns or speech.

education.evidence: Homeschooled and helped change Nevada's home-school laws, serving on the state Home School Advisory Board.

notes: Searched the Independent American Party of Nevada site, which reposts a July 2026 profile of her record; no personal campaign site, questionnaire or debate coverage was found. Positions on welfare, security, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech and faith remain unknown.

name: Gonzalo Duran
current_role: Vice chair of the Bronx Conservative Party
bio: Gonzalo Duran is a military veteran and founder of Devil Dog USA, which helps veterans move into civilian life. He is vice chair of the Bronx Conservative Party and a district leader for the 79th Assembly District, having left the Democratic Party in 2023. He previously ran for Congress in NY-15 in 2024.

platform.point: Restore accountability, personal responsibility and economic opportunity in the Bronx, and oppose socialism.
Support veterans, including those affected by burn pit exposure.
Lists public safety among his core campaign issues.
Lists housing, employment and transportation as campaign priorities for the Bronx.
Calls for more NYPD officers and surveillance in high-crime areas, and a return to beat patrols.
Seeks stronger rules for developers and legislation protecting tenants from steep rent increases.
Would shift tax incentives from large corporations toward local businesses.
Wants stronger oversight of school funds, reasonable class sizes and less reliance on standardized tests.

economy.evidence: Supports stronger developer regulation and rent-increase protections and redirecting corporate tax breaks, while pledging to fight socialism.

security.evidence: Campaign platform calls for expanding the NYPD workforce and surveillance in high-crime neighborhoods.

notes: Reviewed the campaign site's platform pages (safety, housing, education, health, employment, environment, civic engagement) and PoliticsNY coverage; the environment and education pages do not map onto the energy or school-choice scales. No stated positions were found on immigration, foreign policy, tech, faith or social issues.

name: Blay Tarnoff
current_role: Chair of the Nassau County Libertarian Party
bio: Blay Tarnoff is the Libertarian Party nominee for New York's 4th district and chairs the Nassau County Libertarian Party and the Libertarian National Judicial Committee. A Libertarian activist since 1990, he has worked as a computer systems analyst supporting Wall Street analysts and developing neural network systems. He holds a J.D. from Pace University and a mathematics degree from Brown University.

platform.point: Lists freedom, civil liberty and individual liberty among his campaign issues.
Names privatization as a campaign priority.
Lists affordability and controlling inflation as campaign issues.
Lists healthcare reform and the environment among his issues, without published details.

economy.evidence: Lists privatization and personal responsibility as campaign issues; a general statement without specific proposals.

notes: The state party candidate page lists issue headings only; his campaign site (blay.us) returned an access block, and no questionnaires or coverage were found. Positions on all topics except a general economic lean remain unknown.

name: Priscilla Ghaznavi
bio: Priscilla Ghaznavi is running for New York's 7th congressional district on the Our Future line as an independent. Born in Washington, D.C., she has lived in New York for over 30 years and has worked in business and creative leadership roles at several publicly traded companies.

platform.point: Promotes accountable, results-driven leadership that links opportunity and access.
Emphasizes greater public participation in government.
Stresses community organizing and advocacy as a basis for her work.
Calls healthcare a fundamental right with universal access and more mental health services in schools.
Seeks more federal funding for affordable childcare and support for the childcare workforce.
Supports wider access to affordable housing and property taxes tied to income rather than market values.
Supports equal pay and comprehensive reproductive healthcare.
Supports Web 3.0 development with guardrails for transparency, accountability and security.

economy.evidence: Backs expanded federal childcare and small-business capital and income-based property taxes; mostly general statements.

welfare.evidence: General statements: calls healthcare a right that everyone should be able to access and backs more federal childcare investment, without a named program.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, supports comprehensive reproductive healthcare; no positions found on drugs, LGBTQ rights, guns or speech.

tech.evidence: Supports Web 3.0 innovation with transparency and security guardrails, a general statement.

notes: Reviewed the campaign home page and its Community Concerns page; no questionnaires or debate coverage were found. Immigration, foreign policy, energy, security, education choice and faith positions remain unknown.

name: Nathan Weise
bio: Nathan Weise is the Libertarian nominee for Ohio's 1st Congressional District in 2026, named by the Libertarian Party of Ohio to replace its earlier nominee. No further public biographical information was found.

platform.point: Opposes mass license-plate camera networks as warrantless tracking that threatens Fourth and First Amendment rights.
Urges officials at state and federal level to resist government mass surveillance.

security.evidence: Wrote that Flock camera networks amount to warrantless tracking and called for resisting government mass surveillance.

notes: Searched the Libertarian Party of Ohio site, which confirms him as a replacement nominee and carries his statement on surveillance; no campaign website, questionnaire or coverage was found. Positions on all topics except security remain unknown.

name: Thomas McMasters
bio: Thomas McMasters served as mayor of Huber Heights, Ohio, from 2014 to 2018. He ran for Ohio's 10th congressional district as an independent in 2016 and is the Libertarian nominee for the seat in 2026.

platform.point: Focuses on finding inefficiencies in government and reducing wasteful spending.
Says he scrutinizes bill language to catch wording that undermines how a law works in practice.
Says he draws on ideas from across different political philosophies.

notes: Searched the Libertarian Party of Ohio site (listing only) and the prior news article; no campaign website, questionnaire or debate coverage was found, and web search was unavailable in this pass. His general focus on reducing wasteful spending does not map onto any topic scale, so all topics remain unscored.

name: Brennan Barrington
bio: Brennan Barrington is an engineer with a bachelor's degree in aeronautical and astronautical engineering from Ohio State University. He is the Libertarian nominee for Ohio's 15th congressional district in 2026 and has not held elected office.

platform.point: Wants to sharply reduce the scope of the federal government and return authority to states and individuals.
Seeks to eliminate regulations he views as deterring success and expanding bureaucracy.
Favors reforming taxes along Georgist land-value and Pigouvian lines.
Seeks to end redistribution systems he says deter success and misallocate capital.

economy.evidence: Calls for shrinking the federal government and eliminating regulatory systems, while rejecting socialism.

welfare.evidence: General statement: calls for ending redistribution systems he views as discouraging success, without naming specific programs.

notes: His Libertarian Party of Ohio campaign page (barrington.lpo.org) blocked access, so the party's candidate profile remains the main source. He rejects nationalism in general terms, but no specific positions were found on immigration, foreign policy, social issues, energy, tech, education or faith.
